clue.text: 2 succeeding often on the radio — as another?

definitions.text: 2 succeeding often on the radio — as another?

parts.words: 2 succeeding often on the radio — as another?
parts.note: 2 is COMPOSER; said aloud, 'often' sounds like the start of another composer's surname, and this composer's name completes it

explanation.surface: A composer whose music keeps coming up on the radio, perhaps being likened to another.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a composer (2 down) who, placed after a word that sounds like 'often', makes the name of another composer, Jacques Offenbach.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Sebastian Bach is a composer, and Offen plus his surname gives Offenbach, the composer of operettas.

clue.text: Maestro primarily inspired by work in creation of score?

definitions.text: Maestro primarily inspired by work in creation of score?

indicators.note: in says the small built piece sits within the rearranged letters
a creation of the word score is a new thing made from its letters, so they are rearranged
a letter inspired by a word is breathed into it, so it goes inside that word

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work

indicators.note: primarily asks for the first letter of the word Maestro

explanation.surface: A conductor, guided by a piece of music, is creating a score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creation of' rearranges SCORE into COSER, and 'inspired by' puts M inside OP to make OMP, which then sits 'in' COSER. Read as a whole, the clue also describes a composer at work, so it is an &lit.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who writes a score, inspired by a work, is a composer; the whole clue sketches one at their job.

clue.text: Tyrant locking last of opponents in garage

indicators.note: locking means the garage word closes around the single letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a depot is a garage for buses or other vehicles

indicators.note: last of asks for the final letter of the word opponents

explanation.surface: A dictator imprisons the last of his political enemies in a garage.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is an absolute ruler who wields power cruelly, which is what a tyrant is.

parts.note: Miss is the title of a girl or unmarried woman
2 down is COMPOSER, here the American composer Charles Ives

explanation.surface: Written notes received from a woman composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Missives are letters or written messages, so notes in the sense of short written communications.

clue.text: 20 down, 19 and 12 across in Dutch village once

indicators.note: 19 and 12 across are BRAHMS and LISZT; Brahms and Liszt is rhyming slang for drunk, and drunken letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: 20 down is MAHLER, the Austrian composer

explanation.surface: Three composers turn up in an old Dutch settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: Brahms and Liszt is British rhyming slang for 'pissed', meaning drunk, so it signals an anagram of MAHLER. Harlem in New York began as Nieuw Haarlem, a Dutch settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: Harlem in Manhattan was founded as the Dutch village of Nieuw Haarlem in the seventeenth century, before becoming a neighbourhood.

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone feels proved right, or at least partly so, in what they believed.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit a text is to correct it, revising errors and making changes before publication.

indicators.note: securing means the composer's name holds the letter fast inside it

parts.note: 2 down is COMPOSER, here Richard Wagner

explanation.surface: A composer holds on to an elderly chauffeur.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagoner drove a horse-drawn wagon, an occupation now largely historical, so a driver of former times.

clue.text: Quintet and quartet where one might check out 2

parts.note: a quintet is five, V in Roman numerals
a quartet is four, IV in Roman numerals
Aldi is a supermarket chain, a place where shoppers go through the checkout

explanation.surface: Ensembles of five and four players at a venue where one might try out a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check out' suggests examining the music; it is the supermarket checkout, and Aldi is a discount supermarket chain common in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio Vivaldi, the Venetian baroque composer of The Four Seasons, answers 2 down, which is COMPOSER.

indicators.note: drops means the composer's name lets go of the following word, which is removed

parts.note: 2 down is COMPOSER, here Frédéric Chopin

explanation.surface: A composer pops in to buy some meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A chop is a cut of meat, such as lamb or pork, usually including a rib.

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

indicators.note: unfinished says the word for acknowledge loses its final letter

parts.note: to salute someone is to acknowledge them with a gesture

explanation.surface: A cheese left behind, with thanks only half given.
explanation.definitionFit: Port Salut is a mild, semi-soft French cheese originally made by Trappist monks.

clue.text: Ultimately, number being all wrong, take one back

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word number
wrong says the letters of being all are put into the wrong, that is a new, order

explanation.surface: With the figures all mistaken, someone retracts what they said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take one back' looks like retracting a statement; here it means to carry one back in memory.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rings a bell sounds familiar and stirs a memory, so it takes one back to the past.

indicators.note: picking up means catching what is heard, so a word that sounds the same is wanted

parts.note: a list is a written record of items

explanation.surface: A composer collects a record.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt, the Hungarian pianist and composer, answers 2 down, which is COMPOSER.

indicators.note: 19 and 12 across are BRAHMS and LISZT; Brahms and Liszt is rhyming slang for drunk, so the letters reel into a new order

parts.note: 14 down is ELGAR, the English composer

explanation.surface: Three composers out for a drink together.
explanation.walkthrough: Brahms and Liszt is British rhyming slang for 'pissed', meaning drunk, which signals an anagram of ELGAR, as in 5 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Lager is a light, bottom-fermented beer, so a drink in the everyday alcoholic sense.

clue.text: Name gong bagged by more than one of twelve

indicators.note: bagged by means the honour is put into the bag, so it sits inside the word for more than

parts.note: over means more than, as in over a hundred
a gong is British slang for a medal or honour, here the MBE, Member of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A name whose honour is claimed by several people at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More than one' reads as a phrase, but 'more than' gives OVER and 'one of twelve' is the definition. The MBE is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: November is the eleventh month of the year, so it is one of twelve months.

indicators.note: claims means the word for musical talent takes the two letters inside it

parts.note: an ear for music is a musical talent

indicators.note: discontented means emptied of its contents, leaving the outer letters of looking

explanation.surface: A sullen-looking composer is said to have a gift for music.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Edward Elgar, the English composer of the Enigma Variations, answers 2 down, which is COMPOSER.

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a raga is a melodic framework in Indian classical music

explanation.surface: Indian music turned down for being too shaky.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar is a gelatinous substance from seaweed used to set jellies, so a wobbly material.

definitions.meaning: 2 down is COMPOSER, here the American minimalist Philip ...
a flute is a tall narrow drinking vessel, one kind of drinking vessel

explanation.surface: A composer's own flute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flute' looks like the instrument a composer would write for, but it is a champagne flute.
explanation.definitionFit: A champagne flute is a type of drinking vessel, and Philip Glass is a celebrated composer.

parts.note: Goa is a state on the west coast of India
the directors of a company make up its board

explanation.surface: The executives of an Indian state set off on a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: To go aboard a ship or plane is to embark, getting on at the start of a journey.

definitions.meaning: 2 down is COMPOSER, here John ..., known for the silent piece 4'33"
to ... an animal is to shut it up in an enclosure

explanation.surface: A composer is told to be quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shut up' reads as an order to be quiet, apt for the composer of a silent piece, but it means confined.
explanation.definitionFit: John Cage was an American avant-garde composer, and to cage something is to confine it behind bars.

clue.text: Line in solid design of aeronautical engineering triumph

indicators.note: in says the line word is placed inside the solid shape

parts.note: a cone is a solid shape in geometry
a cord is a length of line or string

explanation.surface: A line drawn in a solid blueprint for a famous aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Concorde, the Anglo-French supersonic airliner, was a landmark achievement in aircraft design.

clue.text: Suitcase on bed before end of life — where one pegs out

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after, so the luggage follows the bed

parts.note: a crib is a baby's bed
a bag is a suitcase or other luggage

indicators.note: end of asks for the final letter of the word life

explanation.surface: A suitcase on a bed just before someone dies, where one passes away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pegs out' is British slang for dying, which fits the deathbed picture, but in cribbage the score is kept by moving pegs along a board, and the game ends on pegging out.
explanation.definitionFit: Cribbage is a card game scored on a pegboard; a player pegs out by reaching the final hole and winning.

indicators.note: captivating means holding something captive, so the royal letters sit inside
briefly says the word for the section is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: the brass is a section of an orchestra
HM stands for His or Her Majesty

explanation.surface: Part of an orchestra, briefly enchanting a royal composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Brahms, the German Romantic composer, answers 2 down, which is COMPOSER.

indicators.note: back means the built piece is read backwards
pinned says the word on is fixed in place within the edge word

parts.note: a rim is an edge, and to skirt is to edge, so skirt stands for rim

explanation.surface: A short skirt with something pinned to the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skirt' tempts toward MINI, but here it means to edge round something; 'pinned' puts ON within the edge to make RONIM, and 'back' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Minor means lesser or of little importance, so small in scale or significance.

clue.text: 2: chap stealing hearts, ending in despair

indicators.note: stealing means the word for chap takes the letter into itself

parts.note: a chap is a male
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games

indicators.note: ending in asks for the final letter of the word despair

explanation.surface: A composer, a heartbreaker, ends up in despair.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Mahler, the Austrian late-Romantic symphonist, answers 2 down, which is COMPOSER.

clue.text: On reflection, what one might have said on meeting river with a religious leader

indicators.note: on reflection means seen in a mirror, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.words: what one might have said on meeting
parts.note: hallo is a greeting, what one says on meeting someone
the Tay is the longest river in Scotland

explanation.surface: Someone recalls greeting a river along with a cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: HALLO, TAY and A are read backwards ('On reflection') to give the answer. The Tay is a Scottish river.
explanation.definitionFit: An ayatollah is a high-ranking Shiite cleric in Iran, a senior figure of Islamic religious authority.

indicators.note: without limits means the word loses its first and last letters, its limits

parts.note: an earner is someone who is paid for work

explanation.surface: A composer, one of the salaried, unbounded.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Arne, the English composer of Rule, Britannia!, answers 2 down, which is COMPOSER.

clue.text: 17 across, composer appearing in month — where reason for being late remains unknown?

definitions.text: where reason for being late remains unknown?

indicators.note: appearing in means the pieces show up inside the month abbreviation

parts.note: Oct is the abbreviation for October
17 across is CAGE, and a cage is a pen, an enclosure
Giuseppe Verdi was the Italian opera composer

explanation.surface: A composer turns up during a month, with no one knowing why he is tardy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' suggests lateness for an appointment, but it means dead: an open verdict is a British coroner's finding when the cause of a death cannot be established.
explanation.definitionFit: An open verdict records a death without stating its cause, so the reason the deceased died stays undetermined.

clue.text: Score the finest music, 'Messiah' last of all

indicators.note: last of all asks for the final letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Rating the best of Handel's oratorio as the finest music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' seems to mean a musical score; it means to scratch or engrave.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch a surface is to cut or score lines into it, as an engraver does on metal or glass.

clue.text: Army, one broken from now on

indicators.note: broken means the letters are smashed and reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: One soldier broken by the army from this point onwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Any more, in phrases such as 'not any more', refers to time hereafter, that is from this point forward.
